subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls, and if so should the permanent SDK surface be a raw method-string caller, an allowlisted Gateway request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: The choice changes the public Plugin SDK and the Gateway authorization boundary, so automation should not pick the method exposure, caller-attribution, or compatibility contract.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, documentation, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep only route-scoped dispatch
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls for now and require plugins to use existing HTTP route or capability seams.

options.title: Allow raw Gateway method dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and explicitly accept the larger security and compatibility surface as a product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, documentation, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history signal for Gateway method policy and plugin architecture decisions adjacent to this API boundary.
